races.paceDynamic: Lawmans Blis will take the field along from the front with Prince Hector and Wheres The Crumpet sitting prominent behind him. With only one confirmed pace-setter over this 1m2f trip, the gallop will be steady and sustainable rather than punishing. The lack of early pressure means Lawmans Blis can dictate terms, setting up a tactical finish where positioning becomes crucial. This moderate pace scenario strongly favours hold-up horses who can use their finishing kick, as the lack of early burn-up will leave plenty in reserve for the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Lawmans Blis leads uncontested and the pace stays moderate throughout
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows hold-up horses to conserve energy and unleash their finishing speed. Heartened and Yakhabar benefit most from being able to pick off tiring leaders in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lawmans Blis Wire Job
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays slow and no serious challengers emerge until too late
scenarios.body: Lawmans Blis exploits the lack of pressure to kick clear turning for home before the closers can respond. His recent Catterick win showed he can quicken off a steady pace when getting first run on his rivals.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Injection
scenarios.trigger: If Prince Hector or Wheres The Crumpet apply pressure from the 6f pole
scenarios.body: The increased tempo stretches the field and finds out the stamina reserves over this extended trip. Horses with proven staying power benefit while those dependent on a finishing kick struggle to close the gap.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Tactical Affair
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses converge on the leaders simultaneously in the straight
scenarios.body: The bunched field creates traffic problems and the winner emerges from a scramble rather than tactical positioning. Project Kinsman's fade-in-finish tendency becomes crucial as others get stopped in their run.

watchPoints.text: Project Kinsman's tendency to fade in the finish could prove decisive if the pace is steady and she's still in contention entering the final furlong
Top Flight Century's 301-day absence creates major fitness concerns despite his hurdles win over winter for this yard
Lawmans Blis must handle the surface switch from Catterick's good ground to Newcastle's standard all-weather track
Yakhabar's wind surgery appears to have unlocked improvement based on his Southwell win and subsequent third place
The 8-day gap since Redcar's 1m2f handicap gives Prince Hector, Heartened and Carida potential fitness edge over rivals

races.paceDynamic: Drumcondra is the only confirmed front runner in this field, meaning he can dictate terms without pressure through the early stages of this 1m4½f contest. With Roger Henry and Arch Legend sitting prominent behind, but most of the field preferring to come from off the pace, Drumcondra can set a comfortable rhythm that may not stretch the field sufficiently. The lack of early pace pressure creates a tactical scenario where the leaders can conserve energy for a sustained finish. This race shape clearly favours hold-up horses who can produce their best work late, as they'll get the slow early gallop they need to unleash their finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Drumcondra sets an uncontested lead with no early pressure from the prominent runners.
scenarios.body: The moderate gallop allows hold-up horses to conserve energy and produce telling late runs in the final 2-3 furlongs. Rubellite and Havachoc, both proven closers with strong finishing kicks, can exploit the tactical advantage this creates.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leaders Steal March
scenarios.trigger: If Drumcondra and Roger Henry maintain a genuine gallop that stretches the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: The sustained pace prevents the back markers from making up ground, allowing those racing closer to the pace to maintain their advantage. Roger Henry's prominent style suits this tactical scenario better than the pure hold-up merchants.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Division Move Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes stop-start, creating a bunched finish where positioning matters most.
scenarios.body: A scrappy tactical affair allows horses with tactical speed to find the gaps that matter most in the final furlong. Ned Broy showed this ability when closing strongly at Hamilton, while Desert Quest has course winning form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Maiden Breakthrough
scenarios.trigger: If the exposed handicappers fail to fire and an improving type capitalizes on the weak pace.
scenarios.body: The tactical race setup allows a lightly-raced horse to show hidden ability in these calmer conditions. Drumcondra gets his preferred front-running scenario while Apache Eagle has been consistent in defeat recently.

watchPoints.text: Drumcondra setting too slow a pace early - if the first half-mile is pedestrian, expect a cavalry charge from the closers
Apache Eagle's stalls behavior after Arch Legend previously refused to enter - any loading issues could disrupt the start
Rubellite and Havachoc both holding back too far given their proven finishing kicks - they need to be within striking distance
Desert Quest's jumping ability at the start given his 22-day break and need for sharp beginning from this draw
Roger Henry's fitness levels after 43-day break for new trainer Quinlan who has been finding form recently

races.paceDynamic: Dontwaste A Moment will be the clear pace-setter from stall rise with no other confirmed front-runners in this field. Star Noir, Mystical Land, Golden Havana and Master Harry will all settle prominently behind the leader, creating a bunched group tracking the pace. The sustainable early gallop will set up a sprint finish from the 2f pole as the prominent runners fan out. This tactical setup strongly favours the prominent racers who can track the leader and kick for home, rather than hold-up horses who will struggle to make up ground in a small field sprint.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace remains honest and sustainable throughout
scenarios.body: The prominent quartet get first run on Dontwaste A Moment turning for home and their superior tactical position proves decisive. Golden Havana and Star Noir are perfectly placed to strike in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Dontwaste A Moment kicks clear turning for home and the pace has been modest
scenarios.body: The front-runner gets first run and the prominent horses struggle to reel him in up the short Newcastle straight. His fitness edge from recent running helps him sustain the effort to the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly crawling and turns into a dash
scenarios.body: Pivotal Terms gets the perfect setup from his hold-up style as the field comes back to him in the final 1f. Master Harry also benefits from the sprint finish despite his long absence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Dontwaste A Moment stops quickly and the prominent horses bunch up
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy affair with interference possible as horses change positions mid-race. The most experienced campaigners Golden Havana and Star Noir best navigate the chaos.

watchPoints.text: Dontwaste A Moment could set too strong a pace early and compromise his finishing kick in his first try at 5f
Master Harry's 179-day layoff creates uncertainty about his current fitness levels despite the gear change
Golden Havana's visor retention suggests connections are happy with his recent tactical approach
Star Noir showed signs of pulling hard last time which could impact his settling in the early stages
Pivotal Terms needs a strong pace to be effective but may struggle if the gallop remains modest throughout

races.paceDynamic: Desert Champion looks the sole committed early leader in this 5f sprint, with Jeany May and A Lady Forever likely to press close behind from prominent positions. The pace should be sustainable rather than frantic, as Desert Champion won't face immediate pressure in the opening two furlongs, allowing him to dictate terms. This moderate early gallop will set up a tactical sprint finish where horses with turn of foot can close effectively. The race shape strongly favours hold-up performers who can quicken late, as the pace-setters may lack the sustained speed to hold off closers in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Desert Champion sets uncontested fractions and the pace becomes pedestrian early
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace will allow closers to position perfectly and unleash superior finishing kicks. Horses like Bishop's Glory and What What What can time their runs to perfection when the race becomes a sprint from the 2f pole.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Hold On
scenarios.trigger: If Desert Champion maintains a strong gallop and Jeany May applies early pressure
scenarios.body: The sustained pace will stretch the field and favor those who can travel strongly throughout. Desert Champion's recent Chelmsford win shows he can sustain his effort, while prominent runners may benefit from the honest pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Tactical Battle
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses contest the early lead creating messy positioning
scenarios.body: The disrupted early pace will create gaps and traffic problems, favoring adaptable horses with tactical speed. Runners who can switch off mid-race then quicken when gaps appear will have the advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If Desert Champion goes too slow early allowing the field to bunch completely
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint finish from the 2f marker with positioning crucial. Only horses with genuine turn of foot from the rear will be effective in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Desert Champion may get uncontested lead but his fading tendency could see him weaken markedly in final furlong
Bishop's Glory returning from 124-day layoff - watch market confidence and how sharp he appears in preliminaries
Multiple horses wearing headgear changes including Jeany May's visor - early positioning will reveal effectiveness
Track conditions staying standard throughout card - no advantage emerging for particular running styles
Several 7-day turnarounds including Auntie Jo and Hyrcanian - stamina reserves may be tested late

runners_data.name: Military Leader
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in excellent form with two wins since break, perfectly positioned for this scenario
runners_data.comment: 2-2 since returning from break, winning at Southwell and Thirsk; now a further 3lb higher.

runners_data.name: Chuzzlewit
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse carrying just 120lbs but 38 days since last run may blunt his edge
runners_data.comment: Placed in a Class 4 over C&D (from 10lb higher) last June; steadily regressive since.
runners_data.spotlight: Fine looker, and for all that he's an infrequent winner (2-35), was once rated in the 90s; placed in a Class 4 over C&D (from 10lb higher) last June but he's been steadily regressive since; safer options elsewhere.

runners_data.name: Cusack
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who loves Newcastle with multiple wins here, 5lb claimer provides significant weight relief
runners_data.comment: 10-47 on AW; 3lb below his last winning mark, but seems to have lost his way lately.
runners_data.spotlight: 10-47 on AW, with all bar one of those wins coming at Newcastle (7f-1m2f); now sits 3lb below his last winning mark, and Tom Kiely-Marshall's 5lb claim is a bonus, but seems to have lost his way; may strip fitter for 7f course comeback run.

runners_data.name: Sunriseontheboyne
runners_data.note: Lone pace-setter slipping down handicap, poor recent form suggests vulnerable to pressure
runners_data.comment: Low key in five for this trainer, slipping 9lb in weights, now 1lb below last winning mark
runners_data.spotlight: Won three times in Ireland for Mick Mulvany, including at Listowel (1m, heavy) last September; low key in five starts for new trainer, slipping 9lb in the weights - now 1lb below that last winning mark; needs revival on AW return (3-9).

runners_data.name: Barry's Boy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer won over course and distance from lower mark, hung left under pressure last time
runners_data.comment: Justified favouritism over C&D (3lb lower) penultimate start; settle for minor honours?
runners_data.spotlight: Kept on well to justify favouritism over C&D (from 3lb lower) on penultimate start; beaten - fifth, hung left under pressure - in a stronger Class 4 at Nottingham subsequently; might have to settle for minor honours on AW return.

runners_data.name: American State
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with two wins this year post wind surgery, 37-day break freshens him up
runners_data.comment: Southwell winner (1m; from 4lb lower) on penultimate start; low key at Wetherby since.
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice this year (post wind surgery) for Ivan Furtado, keeping on well at Southwell (1m, Class 5; from 4lb lower) on penultimate start; not at his best at Wetherby (tenth) latest, but there's still a chance he can prove competitive from this revised mark.

runners_data.name: Second Fiddle
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with five course wins but struggles on turf with slow starts recently
runners_data.comment: Five C&D wins; struggled at double-figure odds on turf lately (Musselburgh & Hamilton).
runners_data.spotlight: Five C&D wins, the latest from a 3lb lower mark in December; has struggled at double-figure odds on turf lately (Musselburgh and Hamilton) with slow starts a regular feature; drops back into a Class 5 now at a more suitable track, but with enough to prove for the time being.

runners_data.name: Bellasio
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in good form last year but 11 days since last run very quick for Grant Tuer
runners_data.comment: Fair sixth to Military Leader on Southwell comeback; disappointed at Haydock (1m2f) since.
runners_data.spotlight: In fine fettle (form figure 522122) last spring/summer, rounding off with a close second to Eeetee at Redcar (1m, good to soft, 6-4 favourite) in July; fair sixth to Military Leader on Southwell comeback run but disappointed over 1m2f at Haydock subsequently; best watched.

races.paceDynamic: Sunriseontheboyne is the sole confirmed front runner but faces pressure from five prominent racers: Criminal Shore, Alessia Fernanda, Cusack, Barry's Boy, and Bellasio. This creates a congested early pace with multiple horses wanting the same tactical position just behind the leader. The pace will be honest rather than blazing, but the prominent congestion will create traffic problems and force some wide into the straight. This setup strongly favours the hold-up horses who can avoid the early scrimmaging and exploit the pace collapse when the prominent pack ties up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack gets tangled up fighting for position behind Sunriseontheboyne
scenarios.body: The pace becomes stop-start through the middle stages as five horses jostle for the same real estate, then quickens suddenly. The patient hold-up brigade sweep past tired legs in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one prominent horse finds clear water while the others struggle
scenarios.body: Barry's Boy or Alessia Fernanda position perfectly to avoid the worst traffic while still getting first run on the weakening leader. They maintain momentum while their prominent rivals get shuffled back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Sunriseontheboyne gets an uncontested lead while the prominent pack neutralizes each other
scenarios.body: The leader builds an unassailable advantage while his chasers mark each other out of contention through mid-race positioning battles. He stays clear of the late swooners.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is crawling and becomes a tactical affair throughout
scenarios.body: Nobody wants to commit early, creating a messy sprint finish where barriers and luck determine the outcome. The best turn of foot wins regardless of typical running style.

races.paceDynamic: First Encounter is the sole confirmed front-runner and will likely get an uncontested lead, setting a comfortable tempo with his prominent style. With 13 hold-up horses behind him, there's no early pace pressure, allowing First Encounter to dictate terms through moderate fractions. The lack of early speed means the field will be bunched turning for home, creating a cavalry charge finish where positioning and a clear run become crucial. This race shape strongly favours early positioned horses who can avoid the traffic problems that will inevitably occur when 13 hold-up horses all try to make their moves simultaneously.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Holds
scenarios.trigger: If First Encounter gets soft fractions and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows him to save energy for a sustained finish while the field struggles with traffic behind. His recent wins at similar trips prove he can capitalize on tactical advantages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the bunched field creates severe interference in the home straight
scenarios.body: Multiple hold-up horses get blocked and only those with clear runs can challenge effectively. The leaders escape the carnage while most of the field never gets a proper chance to race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If First Encounter stops quickly after weak fractions and the field closes rapidly
scenarios.body: The slow tempo suits stamina horses who can grind out the finish when the leader weakens. Patient rides on proven stayers become the winning move.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Shock Early Pace
scenarios.trigger: If multiple hold-up horses break their usual pattern and race prominently early
scenarios.body: The unexpected pace battle compromises several runners and allows genuine closers to pick up the pieces. Tactical discipline becomes more valuable than early position.
